title: Ivory Sarees, Chiranjeevi in a Mundu, and Anil Kapoor Dancing: Inside South Cinema's Dreamiest Wedding of the Year
excerpt: Tamannaah and Trisha played bridesmaids, Jackie Shroff wore gold, and half of Indian cinema flew to Goa for Khushbu Sundar's daughter Avantika's wedding — and the photos are everything.
body:
Somewhere on the Goan coast, in a resort draped in white and gold, Avantika Sundar walked towards a mandap flanked by two of South Indian cinema's most luminous women. On her left, Tamannaah Bhatia — serene in an ivory saree, minimal jewellery, hair pulled into a ballet-dancer bun. On her right, Trisha Krishnan — front-row queen, draped in a golden saree and diamond necklace that caught the light every time she turned her head. Between them, a bride about to begin her own story.

Avantika married Shravan Sreenivasan, a Merchant Navy officer from Chennai, on June 25 in what her mother Khushbu Sundar has described as a "love-cum-arranged marriage." Translation: the kids chose each other, then the parents said yes. The resulting wedding was exactly what you'd expect from the daughter of one of South Indian cinema's most formidable couples — actress-turned-BJP-politician Khushbu and filmmaker Sundar C — which is to say, it was extraordinary.

The guest list read like someone had opened every film industry WhatsApp group simultaneously. From Telugu cinema: Chiranjeevi arrived with his wife Surekha, dressed in a traditional veshti that somehow made the megastar look both regal and approachable. Nagarjuna Akkineni came with Amala, wearing teal when everyone else was in gold — because Nagarjuna has always understood that style is about knowing when to break the theme. Venkatesh, eternally steady and warm, rounded out the Telugu contingent.

From Bollywood: Anil Kapoor — because of course Anil Kapoor was there, looking roughly twenty years younger than his birth certificate would suggest, in a white ensemble that somehow drew more eyes than the gold-and-ivory theme. And Jackie Shroff, in traditional South Indian attire, laughing with Chiranjeevi in a viral video that felt like watching two different eras of Indian cinema share a private joke.

One of the most shared moments from the evening was a clip of Jackie Shroff, Anil Kapoor, Chiranjeevi, Venkatesh, and Nagarjuna — five men who have collectively appeared in over a thousand films — sitting together, taking each other's photographs on their phones, laughing like college friends at a reunion. It's the kind of footage that makes you realise how small Indian cinema's inner world really is, how these sprawling industries of hundreds of films a year are actually run by people who genuinely know and like each other.

Trisha, sitting in the front row in conversation with Chiranjeevi and his wife, added an extra layer of intrigue. She's currently the most-Googled woman in Tamil cinema — not just for her devastating turn in Karuppu, which has been one of 2026's biggest South Indian hits, but for the persistent whisper linking her to Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay. The CM, notably, did not attend the wedding, despite Khushbu personally visiting his Chennai residence to deliver the invitation. His absence was diplomatic; Trisha's presence was the louder statement.

The dress code was white and gold, traditional South Indian, and nearly everyone obeyed. Veshtis, mundus, and kanjeevaram silks in muted ivory and burnished gold gave the entire event the air of a heritage Chettinad wedding rather than a typical Bollywood-adjacent spectacle. Tamannaah, who posted a carousel of photos on Instagram with the caption "Fairytales are real, I saw one today," was one of the evening's most photographed guests — not for doing anything particularly dramatic, but for looking like she'd walked out of a Mani Ratnam frame.

For the diaspora watching from screens in New Jersey living rooms and London kitchens, this wedding was a reminder of something easily forgotten: South Indian cinema's social fabric is woven differently from Bollywood's. The guest list crossed linguistic, political, and industry lines. Telugu superstars sat with a Tamil bride's family. Bollywood veterans put on mundus. A BJP politician's daughter married a Merchant Navy officer, and the guest list included everyone from film legends to the crew members who worked on Sundar C's sets.

Avantika herself is no stranger to the camera — she's making her acting debut in the upcoming Malayalam film Aarambham and simultaneously filming a Tamil project called Attacker. But on this particular evening, she was simply a bride in a resort in Goa, with two of the most beautiful women in Indian cinema holding her saree pallu, and a room full of people who've spent their lives making other people's stories clapping for hers.

The photos, predictably, broke the internet. Tamannaah's Instagram post alone pulled over 380,000 likes in under a day. But the image that'll stay longest is probably the simplest one: Tamannaah, Trisha, and their friend Aarti Ravi, all in coordinated ivory, standing shoulder to shoulder with the bride. No red carpet. No brand deal. Just women in sarees, at a wedding, looking happy.

Some things don't need a filter.
